page: Microsoft Azure M64ls is a virtual machine instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 2097 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-threaded capabilities are more robust; bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and large-block memory bandwidth (both read and write) rank in the top 25%. Multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests fall within the middle 50%, showing average performance for parallel workloads.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the presence of 2097 GB of local storage, this instance is structured for memory-intensive and database workloads that can leverage parallel processing. While single-threaded tasks and LLM text generation perform poorly, the system is suited for database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and large memory footprint position it as a resource-dense option for enterprise workloads that require high memory capacity without the need for GPU acceleration.
